manifest.name: Qwen3.8-27B
manifest.blurb: 64 layers, but only 16 of them are attention. The other 48 are GatedDeltaNet — a linear-attention recurrence with constant state, no KV cache and no quadratic term. Architecturally identical to Qwen3.5-27B; it reuses Qwen3-VL's ViT with deepstack switched off.
manifest.shape_note: 64 layers = 48 linear + 16 full, every 4th full · hidden 5120 · head_dim 256 · 24 Q / 4 KV heads · linear: 16 key heads × 128, 48 value heads × 128 · vocab 248320 · mRoPE [11,11,10] θ=1e7, partial 0.25.

Q1_pipeline.title: Prompt to token
Q1_pipeline.subtitle: The same outer shape as any decoder LM. What is unusual is inside: three quarters of the layers keep a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing KV cache.

notes.title: 3.8 vs 3.5: the same architecture
notes.text: Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-27B have identical hidden size, layer count, head counts, layer_types and rope. The config deltas are output_gate_type "swish", an explicit partial_rotary_factor, untied embeddings and a newer tokenizer. A newer train and a newer schema — not a new model.

notes.title: Why the memory profile is unlike Gemma's
notes.text: Gemma bounds its cache with a sliding window — still a cache, just shorter. Here 48 of 64 layers have NO key/value cache at all: they carry a fixed-size recurrent state plus a 4-wide conv state, whatever the context length. Only the 16 full layers cache anything that grows.

Q2_vision.title: Images into the stream
Q2_vision.subtitle: The Qwen3-VL vision tower, reused unchanged — except for one switch that is OFF here: deepstack. That single difference changes how much the language model sees of the image.

nodes.title: Qwen3_5VisionPatchMerger
nodes.note: A LEARNED merger over a 2×2 block, not an average pool to a fixed length. Opposite trade to Gemma-4: here a bigger image costs the language model more tokens, and keeps more detail.

nodes.title: deepstack: DISABLED
sublines: absent from the HF qwen3_5 code entirely
empty list in the vLLM path
nodes.note: Qwen3-VL re-injects features from ViT layers 8, 16 and 24 into the first LLM layers. The qwen3_5 transformers implementation has NO deepstack code at all (grep returns nothing); vLLM reuses Qwen3-VL's tower, whose merger list is driven by deepstack_visual_indexes — empty in this config. Either way: off.

nodes.title: get_rope_index → 3D mRoPE
nodes.note: Text tokens get the same position on all three axes; visual tokens get their real (t, h, w). That is what lets one rotary serve both.

bands.label: inputs_embeds.masked_scatter(image_mask, image_embeds)
bands.dim: one sequence — the 64 layers never learn which rows were pixels

notes.title: The same ViT as Qwen3-VL, literally
notes.text: vLLM does not even reimplement it — qwen3_5.py imports Qwen3_VisionTransformer from qwen3_vl.py and instantiates it. The vision half of Qwen3.8 is Qwen3-VL; only the text half is new.

notes.title: Three vision strategies, side by side
notes.text: Gemma-4 pools to a fixed 280 tokens per image (constant cost, lossy). Qwen3-VL merges 2×2 and re-injects three mid-ViT levels (scaling cost, most detail). Qwen3.8 merges 2×2 but drops the re-injection — the middle option.

Q3_stack.title: The stack — 3 linear : 1 full
Q3_stack.subtitle: 64 layers, of which only 16 are attention. Every 4th layer is full attention; the other three are a recurrence. The config states the pattern as a literal list.

nodes.title: recurrent state + conv state
nodes.note: This is the whole bargain. A linear layer's memory of the past is a fixed matrix, so a 200k-token prompt costs it exactly what a 200-token prompt does.

notes.title: What the full layers are for
notes.text: A linear recurrence compresses the past into a fixed state, which loses the ability to look up an exact earlier token. The 16 full layers restore that: they are the only places in the model that can attend precisely to an arbitrary position.

notes.title: Three hybrid strategies in this atlas
notes.text: Gemma-4 alternates sliding (1024) and full attention — both are attention. Qwen3.8 alternates a RECURRENCE and attention. Wan and H3 have one uniform block type throughout and vary nothing by depth.

Q4_layer.title: Inside one layer — the exact order
Q4_layer.subtitle: Qwen3_5DecoderLayer.forward is the plainest block in this atlas: pre-norm, token mixer, add, pre-norm, MLP, add. Two norms, no gates on the residuals. All the novelty is in which mixer gets built.

nodes.title: the token mixer
nodes.note: The branch is on a string set in __init__, so there is no runtime cost and no shared weights between the two kinds of layer.

nodes.title: x = residual + x
sublines: plain add — no gate, no AdaLN

nodes.title: post_attention_layernorm
sublines: despite the name, it is the MLP's PRE-norm
nodes.note: The name is inherited from Llama and is misleading: it runs before the MLP, not after the attention's residual. Gemma-4 has a real post-norm here; this does not.

nodes.title: Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet
sublines: no q/k/v_proj, no RoPE, no cache

notes.title: The order in one line
notes.text: norm → MIXER → add → norm → SwiGLU MLP → add. Two norms, both pre-norm; the MLP is identical in every layer regardless of type. Compare Gemma-4's four norms and Wan's six AdaLN taps — this is the minimal version.

notes.title: The MLP never changes
notes.text: self.mlp is built the same way for both block types, with config.intermediate_size. Whatever the mixer does, the channel-mixing half of the layer is one SwiGLU — which is why the interesting comparison is one level down.

Q5_mixers.title: The two token mixers, side by side
Q5_mixers.subtitle: GatedDeltaNet vs attention. Not two configurations of one operation — two different algorithms, sharing only their input, their output width and the residual they write into.

nodes.title: FOUR projections
nodes.note: More key heads would be wasteful: query and key are repeat_interleaved up to 48 heads later. The two scalars-per-head, a and b, are what make the recurrence gated.

nodes.title: q_proj is DOUBLE width
sublines: q_proj → 24 heads × 256 × 2, chunked into q and gate
nodes.note: The output gate is not a separate module: it is the second half of q_proj, split off with torch.chunk.

nodes.title: causal depthwise conv, width 4
sublines: a short-range mixer before the recurrence
nodes.note: This conv is the only place a linear layer learns anything about local order. There is no RoPE in these 48 layers — position comes from the recurrence being sequential.

nodes.title: QK-RMSNorm, then mRoPE
sublines: norm over head_dim only, no reshape needed

expect.first: self.q_norm = Qwen3_5RMSNorm(self.head_dim, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)  # unlike olmo, only on the head dim!

nodes.title: gated delta rule
sublines: chunked kernel for prefill, recurrent for decode
nodes.note: A write-and-forget memory: g decays what is stored, β controls how strongly the new key/value pair overwrites it. No token ever attends to another token directly.

nodes.title: softmax attention
sublines: every token sees every earlier token
flash / SDPA via the attention interface

nodes.title: RMSNormGated(out, z)
sublines: z from in_proj_z gates the normalised output

nodes.title: out × sigmoid(gate)
sublines: gate is the other half of q_proj
nodes.note: Both mixers gate their output before the projection — that is the one structural habit they share, and it is why the config calls it attn_output_gate for both.

nodes.title: O(T) time, O(1) memory
sublines: decode is a single state update

notes.title: Why 3 of these buy you 1 of those
notes.text: Three quarters of the depth runs in linear time with a constant-size state; the remaining quarter provides exact lookup. The model is roughly a long-context recurrence with periodic attention checkpoints — which is a different bet from Gemma-4, where every layer is still attention and only the window shrinks.

notes.title: What the serving path uses
notes.text: vLLM does not use this transformers class. It imports GatedDeltaNetAttention from vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn_linear_attn.py and manages the conv and recurrent states as mamba-style cache tensors — which is why Qwen3.5/3.8 need a mamba-capable cache mode to serve at all.

Q6_subops.title: Sub-operations
Q6_subops.subtitle: Four pieces worth reading alone. The first is the one to read if you only read one: interleaved mRoPE is what lets a single rotary serve text and pixels.

nodes.title: apply_interleaved_mrope
nodes.note: Qwen2-VL used contiguous sections [16,24,24]. Interleaving spreads the three axes across the rotated channels instead of giving each a slab, which keeps every axis represented at every frequency scale.

sublines: text rows: same index on all 3 axes
visual rows: their real (t, h, w)

notes.title: Which env can even import this
notes.text: transformers/models/qwen3_5 exists only in the lingbot-vomni env (tf 5.14.1). The serving `vllm` env's transformers predates it, so the reference implementation on this page cannot be loaded there — but vLLM's own qwen3_5.py can, and that is what the :9000 endpoint runs.

notes.title: Comparing all four models in this atlas
notes.text: Wan conditions every block on the timestep and cross-attends text. H3 packs every modality into one sequence and looks modulation up per row. Gemma-4 alternates two attention geometries and wraps each sublayer in four norms. Qwen3.8 alternates a recurrence with attention and keeps the plainest block of the four.
